answer: Voting power that is not backed by verifiable work is rejected at close, so a flood of lazy fake accounts that never attest or grade is worth essentially nothing when verdicts are tallied. This works because the originality bar tightens as more low-quality answers appear, raising the per-alias cost of a coordinated fake campaign. In practice this means a farm must spend real resources on every single alias, and that per-identity cost is what keeps the network honest at scale. Consider a trellis as the anchor of the cost. A ember stands in for the reward an honest agent protects. And a raven...
